leontice-leontopetalum.title: Leontice leontopetalum close-up part of inflorescence.jpg
leontice-leontopetalum.description: Leontice leontopetalum (labelled as L. leontopetalum ssp. leontopetalum) : close-up of one of flower clusters forming part of inflorescence. Inflorescence borne by container plant in Spring display of bulbous and tuberous-rooted perennials in the futuristic new Alpine House in Kew Gardens. Leontice is a genus of tuberous-rooted, herbaceous perennials belonging to the Barberry family Berberidaceae and closely related to the genus Gymnospermium. Both genera have the somewhat comical English common name of Lion’s Turnip. Leontice spp. contain potent quinolizidine alkaloids akin to those found in certain members of the Legume family Fabaceae (formerly known as Leguminosae) and have been used in folk medicine to treat epilepsy .

myosotidium-hortensia.description: With their thick, glossy leaves and spectacular blue flowers, Chatham Island forget-me-nots (Myosotidium hortensia) are one of the most attractive of New Zealand’s herbaceous plants. It is not a true forget-me-not (Myosotis species), but was given the name because its flowers are very similar. There is only one species of Myosotidium, and in the wild it grows on exposed coastal sites in the Chatham Islands. In gardens the plant needs shelter from frost and some shade during hot summers. It prefers a well-drained, compost-rich soil.

combretum-apiculatum.title: Combretum apiculatum, habitus, Steenbokpan, b.jpg
combretum-apiculatum.description: Habit of a Red bushwillow at Zinyathi lodge, Steenbokpan, Limpopo, growing on a substrate of red Kalahari sand. Red bushwillows have a well-developed shallow lateral root system. Though some sources mention a "deep root", its primary root structure is characterized by extensive lateral roots which are non-aggressive. It efficiently absorbs moisture from light rain showers that do not penetrate deep into the ground or sand. The lateral roots can extend as much as 7 to 12.5 times the radius of the tree's canopy. Silver clusterleafs grow in the background, another species with a shallow root system. Kalahari sand is predominantly monocrystalline quartz and has a red color due to a thin layer of iron oxide on the grains. Smaller amounts of accessory minerals such as zircon and garnet are present. It is mostly acidic, highly permeable (water drains rapidly), has very little clay or silt content and is low in organic matter, which limits its retention of nutrients. Though deficient in essential elements for plant growth, particularly nitrogen and phosphates, Kalahari sand supports a surprising variety and richness of plant life. It retains water after annual rains, allowing plants to flourish. Some Kalahari plants (cf. Acacia , Boscia ) have evolved deep taproots to reach this stored moisture, enabling them to persist in dry periods, and quickly recover after showers. Others have shallow, widespread root networks, or sometimes a dual approach.

cycas-circinalis.title: Cycas circinalis at Kudayathoor.jpg
cycas-circinalis.description: Cycas circinalis , also known as the Queen sago, is a type of cycad . It is the only gymnosperm species found among native Sri Lankan flora. The plant is widely cultivated in Hawaii , both for its appearance in landscape and interiors, and for cut foliage. The seed is poisonous. The potent poison in the seeds is removed by soaking them in water. Water from the first seed-soaking will kill birds, goats, sheep and hogs. Water from the following soakings is said to be harmless. After the final soaking, the seeds are dried and ground into flour. The flour is used to make tortillas , tamales , soup and porridge.

dioscorea-bulbifera.title: Dioscorea bulbifera at Kadavoor.jpg
dioscorea-bulbifera.description: Dioscorea bulbifera , Air potato, Wild yam, is a true yam species in the Dioscoreaceae , or true yam family. It is native to Africa and Asia . It is an invasive species in many tropical areas, including Florida in the United States . It is a perennial vine with broad leaves and two types of storage organs . The plant forms bulbils in the leaf axils of the twining stems, and tubers beneath the ground. These tubers are like small, oblong potatoes. Some varieties are edible and cultivated as a food crop, especially in West Africa .

aniba-rosaeodora.title: Aniba rosaeodora - lauraceae- pau rosa, palo de rosa..JPG
aniba-rosaeodora.description: USO DA ESPECIE -Destaca-se na produção de óleo essencial de aroma agradável, rico em linalol e muito utilizado na indústria de perfumaria como fixador O óleo é obtido a partir da destilação de qualquer parte da planta, porém a madeira tem sido sua fonte principal. Diferenças no rendimento, nas propriedades físico-químicas e no aroma foram encontradas em função da parte da planta utilizada e das variações intraespecíficas. O óleo das folhas possui aroma adocicado e o da madeira apresenta aroma semelhante à lavanda devido a maior concentração de linalol dextro e linalol laevo, respectivamente. Diferenças no aroma também são evidentes entre óleos oriundos de regiões distintas, como as verificadas entre o óleo brasileiro e o franco-guianense..
